purpose: A provenance-aware reference model for locating the Solar System in the Milky Way and separating measured astronomy, inferred large-scale structure, procedural expansion, and presentation choices. This is a design contract, not a complete star catalogue or a full N-body simulation.

referenceEpoch.label: J2000-compatible baseline with source-specific observation epochs
referenceEpoch.rule: Do not pretend all source catalogues share one epoch. Store the actual reference epoch and observation epoch per record when available; propagate coordinates using proper motion only when the required data and model are available.
referenceEpoch.gameStartDateMeaning: Campaign narrative reference only; not the astrometric epoch of the Milky Way model.

solarLocation.confidence: well-established broad location; arm boundaries and nomenclature vary by model

componentsToRepresent.geometry: barred central stellar structure; exact dimensions/orientation are versioned parameters

componentsToRepresent.rule: Do not bake one artist's arm outlines as exact physical boundaries; retain alternate/versioned models where useful.

galacticReference.rule: Use a documented Galactic coordinate frame and versioned transformation for actual catalogued positions. This coarse anchor is for galactic-scale map placement only.

orbitalSpeedKilometersPerSecond.note: Published estimates vary by adopted solar galactocentric radius, reference frame, tracers, and model.

motion.simpleCircularApproximationAllowedFor: coarse map preview and rough long-term orientation only
fullSimulationRequirements: versioned Galactic potential or explicitly declared approximation
initial position and velocity in a documented coordinate frame
proper-motion and radial-velocity data when available
separation of stellar orbital motion from spiral-pattern motion
no rigid rotation of every galaxy component as a substitute for dynamics

catalogueStrategy.principle: Use real catalogued objects where available, then expand the universe with deterministic synthetic populations whose provenance clearly says generated.

primaryReferenceCatalogues.name: ESA Gaia
primaryReferenceCatalogues.role: stellar astrometry, photometry, motion, population structure; catalogue selection limits apply

primaryReferenceCatalogues.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive
primaryReferenceCatalogues.role: confirmed planets and published planetary-system data; not a complete census of planetary systems

primaryReferenceCatalogues.name: VizieR Catalogue Service
primaryReferenceCatalogues.role: published astronomical catalogues; each imported catalogue retains its own metadata

catalogueStrategy.mergeRule: Cross-identification may unify multiple catalogue records only with explicit evidence and preserved source identities; never merge solely because names look similar.

proceduralExpansion.whyNeeded: Known catalogues are valuable but incomplete and unevenly sampled. The campaign requires a much larger, internally consistent population than current confirmed-system catalogues can provide.
mustNotDo: label generated stars or planets as observed real objects
silently overwrite measured data with generated values
assume every star has a known planet count
treat catalogue gaps as empty space
use one uniform star density throughout the galaxy
make every generated system habitable or narratively important
mustModelAtAppropriateFidelity: stellar population age and metallicity distributions
gas, dust, and observational selection effects
binary and multiple-star populations where supported by the model
planet occurrence as a distribution with uncertainty, not a universal guarantee
stable object identity independent of render or discovery order
proceduralExpansion.realDataWinsRule: At a matched identity and compatible epoch, accepted measured records take precedence over procedural placeholders. Preserve generated assumptions as provenance if a placeholder was used before import.

motionAndTime.authoritativeState: Object positions are functions of simulation time and a versioned motion model; map rendering never owns or mutates their positions.

motionDomains.model: galactic-potential or explicitly limited coarse approximation
individual measured position and velocity where available; otherwise population model with declared uncertainty
separate pattern-speed/model parameters; do not equate arm pattern motion with each star's orbit
domain-specific model with stated fidelity and validity horizon

motionAndTime.millenniaScaleRule: For a campaign spanning thousands to tens of thousands of years, calculate the actual angular change from the selected model. A simple 230-million-year circular orbit changes by only about 0.016 degrees in 10,000 years; local stellar motion, close encounters, and galactic structure may require separate treatment.
motionAndTime.longTimespanRule: For million-to-hundred-million-year histories, do not merely rotate a static image. Evolve or approximate stars and structures with a declared dynamical model, uncertainty, and fidelity tier.
motionAndTime.historicalReplayRule: Historical map views must specify simulation time, coordinate frame, model version, and whether positions are observed, reconstructed, or illustrative.

representationContract.authoritativeGeometry: Real units, coordinates, distances, uncertainty, and motion remain unchanged by the UI.
allowedPresentationTransformations: logarithmic or nonlinear zoom with a visible scale indicator
screen-space labels and horizon markers for objects outside visual resolution
route ribbons or travel corridors that are explicitly overlays
layer toggles for stars, systems, clusters, dust, hazards, political regions, and history
selection-based exaggeration of visual markers without changing world-space size or separation
forbiddenMisrepresentation: moving objects closer together in authoritative space to improve spectacle
using dense visible asteroid clusters as the default depiction of ordinary space
presenting speculative spiral-arm artwork as a surveyed star-by-star map
showing a travel path as physically navigable without checking drive capability, hazards, and route constraints
hiding the distinction between measured, inferred, and generated objects

navigationHorizon.purpose: Make distant or visually unresolved objects discoverable without pretending they are visible to the naked eye.
navigationHorizon.rule: A marker may be displayed when an object is not optically resolved, but the UI must communicate whether it is seen, sensed, known from a catalogue, or merely predicted.

simulationFidelity.galacticAtlas: versioned statistical structure plus catalogue-backed landmarks
simulationFidelity.cataloguedSystems: measured coordinates and source-aware motion where available
simulationFidelity.generatedSystems: deterministic synthetic population with declared uncertainty and provenance
simulationFidelity.nearbyNavigation: high-fidelity local geometry, motion, sensor visibility, and route constraints
simulationFidelity.historicalGalaxy: time-specific reconstruction with uncertainty; not a present-day image rotated backward

initialValidationGates: Earth resolves to the Solar System and Sun through stable IDs
Sun is marked in the Local/Orion Arm region with coarse placement clearly distinguished from precision coordinates
every imported astronomical record retains source and coordinate-frame metadata
generated objects are visibly and machine-readably distinct from measured objects
catalogue absence never automatically means no object exists
map zoom changes presentation but not world-space distances
historical position queries specify time and model version
10,000-year solar orbital preview does not visibly over-rotate the galaxy
navigation markers distinguish optical visibility from sensor/catalogue/predicted knowledge
procedural population density varies by declared galactic region and population model
openDecisions: canonical Galactic coordinate frame and transformation library
which Gaia release and subsets to import first, including licensing and reproducible download manifests
catalogue storage format, partitioning, and query indexes
galactic potential and spiral-pattern model for long historical intervals
planet population model and confidence calibration
procedural population model parameters and validation datasets
how player-era technology reveals objects beyond direct visual/sensor reach
whether and when the campaign chronology spans millions rather than thousands of years
